claim_text: There is a third type of perception: that of common sensibles (like movement and magnitude) which accompany incidental objects.
rationale: Definitional claim subdividing perception into a three-type taxonomy; referents are grounded in the 428b quote's 'common attributes' and 'incidental objects' denotations (Perception as the genus, common sensibles as the type being posited, incidental perception as the contrast class with which it co-occurs), while the 'third type' taxonomic framing and the 'like movement and magnitude' parenthetical examples in claim_text are extractor-supplied beyond the quote.
notes: PL:ontology-synonymy — ontology has English 'common sensibles' plus Greek slugs 'koina' and 'koina aistheta' for the same concept; labeled the English form per §3.2 decision. | PL:object-of-type-canonicalization — claim_text names 'incidental objects' but the claim's argumentative structure concerns the perceptual type's role (accompanying another type), so canonicalized to 'incidental perception' per §3.2 decision.

claim_text: A point, being simultaneously one and two, is properly said to be divisible.
rationale: Thetic claim about a geometric point's simultaneous unity and divisibility; the three referents (point, unity, divisible) are named in claim_text and grounded directly in the 427a1 quote, each passing the §3.0 node-choice principle (concept-match at correct abstraction level, no richer alternative). The analogical targets of the deployment in 3.2/3.3 (Time, discriminating faculty) are flagged as implicit referents rather than labeled; the predicated 'two' has no canonical node at the correct level of abstraction and is flagged AF4.
notes: AF4:two (numerical duality) — no ontology node at the correct level of abstraction for the Aristotelian technical concept of ἀριθμός / πλῆθος; 'number' is broader, 'discrete plurality' / 'numbers' / 'plurality' are all too broad and thin (see drift-log 2026-04-22 slug-graveyard entry for the seven-slug research result). | AF5:Time — analogical target at 427a1; the claim is deployed to illuminate how the time of discrimination (a moment) is simultaneously one and two hence divisible, but Time is not named in claim_text. | AF4:discriminating-faculty — no richly-canonical node; 'krisis', 'kritikon', 'to kritikon', 'discrimination', 'judgement' all exist only as thin slugs that are also broader than the Aristotelian τὸ κρῖνον technical sense. | AF5:discriminating-faculty — analogical target at 427a1; the point's one-and-two-hence-divisible structure illuminates how a single discriminating faculty can grasp contraries without losing unity, but the faculty is not named in claim_text.

claim_text: When we merely imagine something fearful or encouraging, we remain emotionally unaffected, like viewers of a painting.
rationale: Empirical observation relating two psychological powers: under mere imagination (without doxastic commitment), no emotional affection is produced. Imagination and Emotion are the referents named in claim_text, each a rich canonical grounded in the 427b22 quote; the painting is an illustrative analogy and not a referent; the implicit contrast with opinion/doxa (the judgmental take-as-true state that does produce emotion, per nearby claim-032) is flagged AF5 rather than labeled under the strict-surface rule.
notes: PL:ontology-synonymy — ontology has rich canonicals Imagination (φαντασία) and Emotion (πάθος) alongside thin slugs (phantasia; pathos, affection) for the same two concepts; labeled the rich English forms per §3.2 decision. | AF5:opinion — elided contrast supplied by 427b22 context via 'merely imagine' (the contrasted state is taking-something-to-be-fearful, i.e. the doxa/judgment state that does produce emotion per nearby claim-032); held back from expected_ontology_nodes under strict-surface rule. The 'opinion' slot is thin and sits within a 13-slug opinion/doxa/hupolepsis concept-cluster with no rich canonical among them; see drift-log 2026-04-22 for the second slug-graveyard instance counted against the item-007 pattern-watch.

claim_text: Actual sensation can produce a movement that is necessarily similar in character to the sensation itself.
rationale: Thetic claim at 428b1 stating a causal relation that functions as part of the definition of phantasia: actual (energized) sensation produces a movement (= phantasia, per the definitional frame established at claim 052) that is necessarily similar in character to the sensation itself. Surface referents in claim_text are Perception (the active sensation as cause), Actuality (the energeia qualifier distinguishing active from potential sensation, load-bearing for the claim), and Movement/Change (the produced kinesis). Imagination (phantasia) is flagged AF5 as the claim-internal implicit referent: the indefinite article 'a movement' functions as definite reference to the specific kind of movement the passage is defining, though phantasia itself is not named in this claim_text.
notes: PL:ontology-synonymy — three synonymy cases in this one claim: (a) Perception (rich, αἴσθησις) + aisthesis (thin slug) for the same concept, English form labeled per §3.2 decision. (b) Movement/Change (rich, no-spaces, DA-emphasized def including 'phantasia defined as a kinesis') + Movement / Change (rich, with-spaces, Physics-emphasized def distinguishing kinesis from energeia) + kinesis (thin slug) — two rich canonicals for the same concept; labeled the no-spaces variant because its DA-specific definition matches the 428b1 passage context per §3.0 (rich-preferred-by-context-match). (c) Actuality (rich, ἐνέργεια) + Actuality / Fulfilment (rich, engages energeia-vs-entelecheia refinement) + three thin slugs (energeia, actuality (ἐνεργείᾳ), actuality (ἐντελέχεια)) — labeled Actuality because the claim deploys the energeia-vs-dunamis contrast without engaging the energeia-vs-entelecheia refinement. | AF5:Imagination — claim-internal implicit referent; the indefinite 'a movement' functions as definite reference to phantasia in the definitional context of 428b1 (cf. claim 052: 'imagination is held to be a movement and to be impossible without sensation'). Imagination has a rich canonical (φαντασία) but is not named in claim_text, so flagged AF5 rather than labeled under strict-surface.

claim_text: If actual imagination were identical to actual sensation, imagination would exist in all animals, but it is not thought to.
rationale: Dialectical refutation (reductio) at 428a8: if actual imagination and actual sensation were identical, imagination would universally accompany sensation and thus be present in all brutes; the empirical observation that ants, bees, and grubs lack imagination (per nearby claim-038) refutes the antecedent identity thesis. Referents are Imagination and Perception (the two faculties whose identity is being denied), Actuality (the energeia qualifier distinguishing active from potential states, load-bearing for the specific form of the thesis — Aristotle is not refuting identity of the mere capacities), and brutes (the class over which the first consequent universally quantifies; claim_text 'animals' is a paraphrase broadening of Greek θηρία, which specifically means non-rational animals — labeled brutes per §3.0 concept-match, since Aristotle's empirical counter-evidence applies only to non-rational animals). The 'identity' relation operates structurally in the reductio but is not a posited referent and not labeled. No AF5 flag: the reductio's implicit warrant (universal-over-animals inference) and implicit empirical fact are argumentative propositions, not conceptual implicit-referents.
notes: PL:ontology-synonymy — four synonymy cases in this one claim: (a) Perception (rich, αἴσθησις) + aisthesis (thin slug); (b) Imagination (rich, φαντασία) + phantasia (thin slug); (c) Actuality (rich, ἐνέργεια) + three thin variants (energeia, actuality (ἐνεργείᾳ), actuality (ἐντελέχεια)) — labeled Actuality as at item 053 because the claim deploys the energeia-vs-dunamis contrast without engaging the entelecheia refinement; (d) animals (thin, claim_text surface) + brutes (thin, source-Greek concept θηρία) — labeled brutes per §3.0 concept-match because claim_text 'animals' is a paraphrase-broadening and Aristotle's actual argument targets non-rational animals specifically (ants/bees/grubs per claim-038). Observation: the ontology's 'animal'-prefixed namespace contains 15+ thin-slug entries for related-but-distinct concepts (animal activity, animal cognition, animal soul, animalia imperfecta, etc.) — does NOT count as a slug-graveyard instance because the sibling nodes denote distinct concepts rather than the same concept, but worth noting for upstream ontology curation.

claim_text: Sensations are always true, while imaginations are mostly false.
rationale: Dialectical premise at 428a11 endorsed by Aristotle (per source-record stance) asserting an asymmetric truth-value distribution across two perceptual faculties: sensations are always true, imaginations are mostly false. The four referents (Perception, Imagination, true, false) are all named in claim_text as the subjects and predicates of the parallel contrastive predications. The claim is deployed as a premise in the larger reductio refuting the phantasia=aisthesis identity thesis (per source-record warrant: 'if sensation and imagination have different truth-values, they cannot be identical'), but the identity thesis is passage-level argumentative purpose, not claim-internal content — no AF5 flag here; compare item 053 where phantasia WAS AF5-flagged because the claim was itself a move IN the definition of phantasia.
notes: PL:ontology-synonymy — four synonymy cases: (a) Perception (rich, αἴσθησις) + aisthesis (thin slug); (b) Imagination (rich, φαντασία) + phantasia (thin slug); (c) true (thin, English adjective) + alethes (thin, Greek transliteration) — no Aristotelian rich canonical available for this concept; labeled the English-adjective surface form per §3.2 decision; (d) false (thin, English adjective) + falsehood (thin, English noun) + pseudh (thin, Greek transliteration) — labeled 'false' per surface-match to claim_text adjective and §3.2 English-form preference. Observation — wrong-context rich canonical: the ontology has a rich 'Truth' node but its definition is explicitly Heideggerian (aletheia-as-unconcealment per Being and Time), not Aristotelian correspondence-truth; labeling 'Truth' here would be mis-denotation under §3.0 concept-match. Registered as pattern-watch wrong-context-rich-canonical in drift-log 2026-04-22, with retrospective observations for item 033 (Fear rejected as Heideggerian Furcht) and item 037 (animal rejected as Heideggerian-context slug).
